record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: Can one avoid abelian cubes uvw with |u| = |v| = |w| >= 2 over a binary alphabet?

evidence.quote: Can we avoid abelian-cubes of the form uvw, with |u| =|v| =|w|>= 2, over a binary alphabet?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma = \{a,b\}$ be a binary alphabet, and let $\Sigma^*$ denote the set of all finite words over $\Sigma$. Two words $x,y \in \Sigma^*$ are said to be abelian-equivalent (written $x \sim_{ab} y$) if they have the same length and, for every letter $c \in \Sigma$, the number of occurrences of $c$ in $x$ equals the number of occurrences of $c$ in $y$. A word $w$ is called an abelian cube if $w = uvw'$ for some nonempty words $u, v, w' \in \Sigma^*$ with $|u| = |v| = |w'|$ and $u \sim_{ab} v \sim_{ab} w'$. An infinite word $\mathbf{x} \in \Sigma^{\mathbb{N}}$ is said to avoid abelian cubes of period at least $2$ if $\mathbf{x}$ contains no factor of the form $uvw'$ with $|u| = |v| = |w'| \geq 2$ and $u \sim_{ab} v \sim_{ab} w'$.

Question: Does there exist an infinite word over the binary alphabet $\{a,b\}$ that avoids abelian cubes of period at least $2$?
artifact.status_search_result: The literature distinguishes this from the related $k$-abelian cube problem: it is established that $k$-abelian cubes are avoidable over a binary alphabet for $k \geq 3$ (Mercaş–Saarela), but the question of avoiding ordinary abelian cubes $uvw$ with $|u|=|v|=|w|\geq 2$ over a binary alphabet appears to remain unresolved in the surveyed sources. Some references suggest such abelian cubes of period at least 2 are unavoidable on binary, but no definitive published proof was located in this search.

status_evidence.title: 3-Abelian Cubes Are Avoidable on Binary Alphabets
status_evidence.snippet: It was proved that k-abelian cubes are avoidable on binary alphabets for k>=3.
status_evidence.claim: The k-abelian variant has been resolved for k>=3, leaving the ordinary abelian-cube case as a separate question.

status_evidence.title: 5-Abelian cubes are avoidable on binary alphabets
status_evidence.snippet: Avoidance of k-abelian cubes for k>=5 on binary alphabets.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms progress on k-abelian variants but does not settle ordinary abelian cubes with parts length >=2.

status_evidence.title: Avoidability of long k-abelian repetitions
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses long abelian and k-abelian repetitions on binary and other alphabets.
status_evidence.claim: Surveys the avoidability landscape; ordinary abelian cubes with period >=2 on binary remain a delicate question.
